proposal: The Mandate recommends air permitting reforms: ensure that efficiency improvements to a production process do not trigger new permitting requirements, revisit assumptions that sources run continuously (which inflate potential to emit and permit terms), defend the position that Title V petitions should not second-guess earlier state decisions, and clarify the relationship between New Source Review and Title V so Title V is used only as Congress intended (pp. 426-427). The Once-In, Always-In item on the same page is tracked separately.
remaining: The Title V final rule takes effect on 2026-10-26 (final but not yet effective as of 2026-10-15; p. 427)
A final rule on begin actual construction (proposal only as of 2026-10-15)
Any rule or policy revisiting continuous-operation assumptions in potential to emit (p. 426; none found)
Efficiency-project reforms ensuring no new NSR triggers (p. 426); the 2025 withdrawal removed a tightening proposal rather than adding a reform

flags: Progress lowered from 50 to 40 (stage stays in_progress): the Title V rule is final but not yet effective and squarely covers two of the four elements (NSR and Title V relationship, Title V petitions and earlier state decisions); the potential-to-emit element has no action and the efficiency element has only a withdrawal of a tightening proposal plus an unrelated-in-scope begin actual construction proposal.

Judgment call: proposed 20 would be defensible until the Title V rule takes effect on 2026-10-26; after that date progress near 45 to 50 would be defensible. The rubric puts a final but not yet effective rule at in_progress, so in_progress is kept.

status_summary: On 2025-07-21 EPA withdrew the prior administration's May 2024 proposal on project emissions accounting for New Source Review, citing burden on sources and agencies. On 2026-05-13 EPA proposed to revise the definition of begin actual construction so non-emitting construction could start before a permit is issued. On 2026-09-25 EPA published a final rule, effective 2026-10-26, codifying that its Title V oversight generally will not be used to review New Source Review requirements and that it generally does not reevaluate final preconstruction permits through Title V petitions. No rulemaking on potential-to-emit assumptions was found.

timeline.event: EPA published a notice withdrawing its 2024-05-03 proposed rule on project emissions accounting for Prevention of Significant Deterioration and nonattainment New Source Review (90 FR 34206).
EPA sent a letter to the Maricopa County Air Quality Department on the meaning of begin actual construction for a semiconductor facility core and shell, as described in the later proposed rule.
EPA proposed to revise the definition of begin actual construction in the PSD and nonattainment NSR rules, adding a definition of pollutant-emitting activities (91 FR 26958; comments due 2026-06-29).

EPA published a final rule, effective 2026-10-26, clarifying the scope of applicable requirements under Title V, generally not reviewing NSR requirements through Title V or Title V petitions and excluding the section 112(r)(1) general duty (91 FR 61026).

title: Reform New Source Review and Title V permitting: efficiency projects, PTE, Title V scope
uncertainties: The Title V final rule was read only to character 100000 of about 119000, and the withdrawn 2024 proposal is described from the withdrawal notice. The withdrawn 2024 proposal was a prior-administration proposal that would have tightened project definitions, so its withdrawal is aligned with, not identical to, the efficiency-project recommendation. Searches run: Federal Register API (project emissions accounting, begin actual construction, potential to emit, Title V), plus one web search on begin actual construction guidance. Law-firm commentary on a September 2025 guidance was seen in search results but not read, and is not used. Review confirmed that the Title V rule discusses petitions to object and states that since 2017 EPA has generally not reevaluated final preconstruction permits through Title V. Once-In, Always-In is tracked in c13-14.
